findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:938-943,1012-1018,1189-1191 — defer-with-proof gate contradiction: Path C promises that every known or uncertain protected-surface risk must complete Red -> root cause -> fix -> Green in the current Story regardless of assigned severity, but the only authoritative predicate first requires policy.effectiveBlockingSeverities.includes(finding.severity) and its inputs contain no protected-surface state. A low/medium protected-surface Finding excluded by the current severity policy therefore returns non-blocking before applicabilityAndDispositionBlocks runs; protectedSurfaceImpact exists only inside a deferral record, which an ineligible Path-C Finding will not have. The Story tests repeat the promise without specifying a gate-consumed protected-risk fact or severity-elevation rule. Define a signed protected-surface classification available for every applicable Finding and make the shared predicate enforce it independently of ordinary severity/round decay (or narrow the prose to mere deferral ineligibility); otherwise the advertised mandatory Red-to-Green safety floor is not mechanically expressible.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f741bf8754: section 7.1 now defines a signed MandatoryRepairClassification checked before status, severity, and round decay; protected-surface known/unknown/missing evaluation creates the non-decaying floor and resolve/dismiss requires fresh closure evidence.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:549,678-704,795-835,904-925,976-1010 — signed route acceptance is a mandatory safety input but no RouteReceipt contract exists. CandidateRoute and FindingDeferralDisposition carry only routeReceiptId; FindingLedgerReceipt proves persistence and explicitly does not attest content truth, while no modeled record binds the candidate/finding/deferral, target Story or B-META gap, owner identity/authority, acceptance decision, freshness, signature, and revocation/closure state. append_route_receipt and atomic-commit prose therefore cannot establish the repeated claim that the existing target/owner accepted the route, and the gate/scorecard cannot validate owner acceptance without inventing semantics in implementation. Add an explicit signed RouteReceipt schema plus writer authority, validation/freshness/revocation rules, references from the manifest and ledger receipt, and Story 2/3 ownership/tests; otherwise defer-with-proof can degrade into an unowned waiver despite the stated policy.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f741bf8754: FindingRouteReceipt now binds exact source subject, target state/scope, target-authorized owner/lease/policy, decision, expiry/revocation, policy digest, hash, and signature; section 7.3 defines authority and freshness.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:548-580,678-704,816-820,1004-1010 [high] route-authority gap: defer-with-proof can clear an otherwise-blocking verified Finding only when a signed routeReceiptId proves the target/owner accepted the route, but the plan defines no RouteReceipt record, signer/eligible accepting authority, target-state/hash binding, or verifier contract. Finding Ledger Integrity explicitly proves persistence only and disclaims routing judgment; Candidate and Defect Identity owns advisory routing only; Dynamic Applicability only defines assessment/deferral authority. A bare ID therefore cannot mechanically prove owner acceptance and leaves a circular/unowned L4 dependency that an implementation could fabricate or validate inconsistently. Define the receipt schema and authority boundary, assign its semantic writer/verifier to Story 1 or Story 2 while Story 3 owns only atomic persistence, and add tamper/wrong-target/wrong-owner/stale-target negative tests before allowing deferral to affect the gate.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f741bf8754: Story 1 owns route semantic acceptance/signer/verifier and target-authority validation, Story 3 owns atomic persistence only, and Story 2 consumes fresh receipts for advisory recall.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:938-964,1012-1018,1189-1191 — the promised mandatory repair for every verified applicable high Finding conflicts with the explicitly preserved round-decay predicate. isDynamicFindingBlocking still applies !isAdvisoryThisRound before the disposition decision, and the current advisory contract makes high advisory from Round 3 onward; section 7.1 also says current round-decay semantics continue. Consequently an unfixed high Finding can clear the blocker through round decay without any deferral, Red/root-cause/fix/Green, contradicting Path C and Story 1 acceptance. Critical does not decay, but high does. Either define and register a non-decaying mandatory-repair class/fact for applicable high and protected-surface Findings, or narrow the Red-to-Green promise to critical/currently blocking severities and state that high still follows existing decay. The present plan cannot simultaneously preserve decay and guarantee high repair.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f741bf8754: applicable high/critical mandatory repair is explicitly non-decaying; current round decay applies only outside the mandatory floor, and warn rollback restores the old predicate.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:938-943,1012-1018 [high] The shared predicate applies effectiveBlockingSeverities and round decay before applicability/deferral, so a high Finding becomes advisory in Round 3 and a low/medium protected-surface Finding can remain non-blocking even though Path C says every high/critical or protected-surface risk must be fixed with fresh Green before the blocker clears. Refusing deferral cannot enforce mandatory repair when the old predicate has already returned false. Specify one mechanically enforceable rule: either preserve existing decay and narrow the Path C claim to only prevent defer_with_proof, or add a registered protected/high hard-floor predicate with tests showing all consumers agree and rollback restores the prior rule.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f741bf8754: shared predicate checks mandatoryRepairFloorBlocks first and tests cover severity-policy, round-decay, and direct-status bypass for high/protected cases.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:678-704,793-836,902-922 [high] CandidateRoute and FindingDeferralDisposition require a signed routeReceiptId proving target/owner acceptance, but the data model defines no RouteReceipt contract, signer, authority, target/owner binding, acceptance status, or freshness validation. FindingLedgerReceipt only records an append_route_receipt operation, has no signature, and proves persistence rather than target acceptance. This leaves the gate-critical anti-waiver proof uninterpretable and the three-Story ownership incomplete. Define the signed accepted-route receipt schema and assign its acceptance writer/verifier to Story 2 or Story 1 while Story 3 owns only atomic persistence; test wrong target, wrong owner, stale/closed target, forged signer, and atomic rollback.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f741bf8754: signed FindingRouteReceipt schema, target-side signer authority, wrong-target/owner/signer and stale/revoked/tampered negative tests, plus Story 1/2/3 ownership are explicit.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:707-721,793-823,988-1008 [medium] Deferral says root-cause analysis may remain for the target Story, yet every deferral requires canonicalDefectId and the only CanonicalDefect contract requires a concrete rootCause string. A new reproduced defect with unknown root cause cannot satisfy both contracts without fabricating a placeholder or doing the work deferral is meant to postpone. Make the dependency implementable by allowing an explicitly unresolved canonical identity state/rootCause, or require deferral to reference an already-confirmed canonical defect whose root cause is known and state that narrower eligibility in the tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f741bf8754: CanonicalDefect now has rootCauseState unknown|hypothesized|confirmed with optional rootCause; unknown identity uses trigger/reproduction/contract evidence and later correction is append-only supersession.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:699-704,831-836,1009-1010,1468-1471 [high] CandidateRoute and deferral require only that expiresAt is present/non-expired; no maximum TTL, policy binding, ordering constraint, or periodic next-check cadence is specified. expiresAt=9999-12-31 therefore passes the written completeness metric and can turn defer-with-proof into the effectively permanent waiver the plan forbids when no event trigger fires. Bind expiry to a reviewed policy digest with a finite maximum TTL, validate createdAt < expiresAt <= policy ceiling, and add boundary/clock/overdue tests plus exactly-once recall.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f741bf8754: signed DeferralExpiryPolicy V1 caps medium at 7 days and low/hard ceiling at 30 days, validates timestamps, forbids in-place renewal, and requires boundary/overdue/exactly-once recall tests.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1408-1429,1513-1549,1643-1661 [high] route-receipt ownership introduces a Story 1 <-> Story 2 cycle: Story 1 is the sole semantic FindingRouteReceipt signer/verifier and requires Story 2 accepted/merged plus consumes Story 2 CandidateRoute, while Story 2 deliverables/tests require an accepted fresh Story 1 route receipt before CandidateRoute/recall can pass. Story 2 therefore cannot satisfy its acceptance before Story 1, contradicting the declared Story 3 -> Story 2 -> Story 1 DAG and leaving CandidateRoute acceptance unavailable at Story 2 completion. Move the non-gating target-acceptance receipt contract/signer-verifier needed by CandidateRoute into Story 2 (with Story 1 later consuming and registering it as an L4 deferral dependency), or explicitly split advisory candidate-route acceptance from gate-bearing deferral acceptance with an acyclic interface and tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 043feddaa3: Story 2 now independently owns the non-gate target-side FindingRouteReceipt contract, signer/verifier and freshness; Story 1 only consumes the finding_route profile and binds its exact hash into L4 deferral, while the dependency verifier forbids Story 2 importing Story 1.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:906-931,1190-1207,1270-1279,1485-1489,1790,1892,1965-1967 — finite-expiry/root-cause contract has an indefinite-renewal loophole. V1 caps each medium row at 7 days and each low row at 30 days, but renewal merely requires a fresh assessment, target acceptance, and superseding deferral; the schema and validators define no cumulative age from the first deferral, renewal-count ceiling, target progress/root-cause evidence, or escalation to mandatory repair. A target can therefore accept a new 7/30-day row forever while every per-row timestamp, policy, freshness, and scorecard check passes. This contradicts the risk claim that the hard 30-day ceiling prevents an open applicable defect staying advisory forever and leaves rootCauseEvidenceRefs optional without any time-linked strengthening. Define a lineage-wide cumulative ceiling or bounded renewal count and require progress/root-cause evidence (with explicit escalation to mandatory repair or refusal when absent) before renewal; add deterministic chain tests and a cumulative scorecard denominator. Per-row immutable supersession alone does not make deferral finite.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 043feddaa3: the canonical deferral lineage has an immutable earliest firstDeferredAt, strictest observed severity, cumulative horizon and renewal count; medium is capped at seven cumulative days with zero renewals, low at thirty days with at most one target-authorized progressed renewal, after which mandatory repair is emitted.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1408-1429,1513-1549,1643-1661 [high] The declared Story 3 -> Story 2 -> Story 1 order is not implementable with the current route-receipt ownership. Story 1 exclusively owns the FindingRouteReceipt semantic commands/signer/verifier and may only run a read-only, no-authoritative-write prototype before its prerequisites, while Story 2 requires a fresh accepted Story 1 route receipt for CandidateRoute and recall acceptance tests. Therefore Story 2 cannot be accepted before Story 1, yet Story 1 enforce requires Story 2 accepted and merged. Split a non-gating target-acceptance receipt interface into Story 2, or introduce an explicit prerequisite foundation with acyclic ownership; Story 1 can then add the L4 deferral/gate consumer without circular acceptance.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 043feddaa3: the enforce dependency is now acyclic Story 3 to Story 2 to Story 1; Story 2 supplies standalone non-gate route semantics and explicitly cannot import any Story 1 command, artifact or handler.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:914-927,1203-1207,1270-1279,1426-1427,1485-1489,1790,1892,1965-1967 [high] The claimed hard TTL ceiling is only per deferral row. Renewal requires a new assessment, target acceptance, and superseding row, but the schema/policy defines no lineage-wide maximum elapsed time, renewal-count ceiling, required target progress/root-cause evidence, or escalation after repeated renewal. An applicable low/medium defect can therefore remain non-blocking forever through a chain of individually valid 7/30-day rows while all written validators and metrics pass. Add a cumulative horizon anchored to the first deferral or a bounded renewal count, plus progress evidence and fail-closed escalation/refusal, and test/score complete renewal chains rather than only each row.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 043feddaa3: severity, target, owner, Story, canonical supersession, merge, split and new deferral rows cannot reset lineage age or renewal count; renewal requires changed target-authorized progress evidence, and exhaustion or tamper fails closed into mandatory repair with exactly-once recall.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:946-1000,1039-1060,1296-1304,1492-1494 [high] exact-receipt binding is promised but absent from the gate-bearing schemas: FindingDeferralDisposition.target and FindingDispositionManifest store only routeReceiptId, while the plan says Story 1 binds the exact Story 2 receipt hash into the signed L4 deferral. Without routeReceiptHash plus an expectedRouteReceiptHash/CAS field in the manifest, the deferral signature cannot mechanically bind the verified receipt bytes and the batch apply cannot detect ID-to-content mismatch/substitution at decision time. Add the exact receipt hash to the deferral and manifest disposition, include it in deferralHash/manifestDigest/signatures, and require ID+hash+profile+source-assessment hash equality with stale/revoked/superseded negative tests. F-009s dependency cycle is otherwise closed: Story 2 is independently testable and every receipt remains standalone non-gate.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 9d96f86af9: FindingDeferralDisposition now signs routeReceiptId, routeReceiptHash, finding_route profile, source-assessment hash and target snapshot; manifest actions sign the corresponding expected tuple and apply validates it against latest-chain bytes in the same CAS transaction.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1113-1134,1163-1174,1237-1248,1339-1344 [high] Exhausted or invalid deferral lineage is promised as a non-decaying mandatory floor, but the first mandatoryRepairFloorBlocks call is not given deferralState/lineageState. Exhaustion is otherwise handled only by applicabilityAndDispositionBlocks after status, effective severity, evidence, and round short-circuits, where a low or round-decayed medium Finding returns non-blocking. The prose assumes a MandatoryRepairClassification is emitted at the clock boundary, but a missing/failed/racing append leaves the predicate no input from which to infer that this classification is required. Pass a derived signed/validated lineage exhaustion state into the first floor predicate (or make the floor reader derive it directly), and test missing classification/write failure at exact expiry, over-count, tamper, and severity-transition boundaries; fallback to the previous predicate is not fail-closed for low/decayed medium.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 9d96f86af9: verifier-derived DeferralLineageState is the first shared-predicate floor; missing, expired, exhausted, tampered or unknown-at-boundary claimed lineage blocks before status, severity, evidence or round policy even when classification audit append is absent, fails or races.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:723-776,1293-1294,1324-1333 [medium] progressEvidence is not mechanically replay-resistant. Its schema contains only previousDeferralId, free-form evidenceRefs, and progressDigest; it has no admissible evidence kind, referenced evidence hash/signature, producedAt, target/head/material binding, or predecessor baseline digest. Consequently the requirement that evidence be created after the predecessor and materially changed cannot be proven from the receipt: stale or cross-target refs, reordered refs, or a newly signed digest over unchanged bytes can satisfy the shape. Define canonical server/CLI-derived progress input tuples and digest comparison against the predecessor target snapshot, require referenced signed target evidence newer than the predecessor and current at renewal, and add replay/reorder/cross-target/stale-evidence negative tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 9d96f86af9: typed ProgressEvidenceBinding signs evidence ID, hash, signature and producedAt, full target snapshot, previous deferral and predecessor baseline in a canonical tuple digest; stale, cross-target, reordered, replayed and re-signed unchanged evidence is explicitly rejected.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:946-1000,1039-1060,1296-1304,1492-1494 [high] Route authority regresses at the gate binding: the prose requires Story 1 to bind the exact Story 2 receipt hash, but FindingDeferralDisposition.target and FindingDispositionManifest store only routeReceiptId. Neither signed structure carries routeReceiptHash/expectedRouteReceiptHash, so a manifest apply cannot CAS-check the bytes that were verified against ID substitution, stale-chain resolution, or a concurrent revoke/supersede. Add the receipt hash to both signed deferral and manifest disposition and validate ID+hash+profile+source-assessment hash plus latest-chain freshness atomically. This independently corroborates open F-013.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 9d96f86af9: both L4 deferral and manifest bind exact receipt ID, hash, profile and source assessment; same-transaction latest-chain freshness and revoke/supersede CAS failure writes neither deferral nor manifest action.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1227-1228,1296-1305,1492-1494,1597-1601,1712-1716,1806-1807 [high] The route-ownership cycle is removed at the API/DAG level, but the transaction contract still requires mutually incompatible write ordering. Story 2 now independently persists every non-gate FindingRouteReceipt and Story 1 consumes an already-available receipt; warn explicitly permits standalone Story 2 receipt writes. Yet Path B says the route and deferral commit atomically and neither may exist alone, and Story 3 tests require a deferral plus its prevalidated route/receipt to commit together or leave neither visible. Story 2 cannot both be independently accepted with durable standalone receipts and defer their first persistence until a later Story 1 transaction. Define one acyclic boundary: persist the Story 2 receipt independently, then have Story 1 atomically CAS-validate its exact latest ID/hash/profile/source and append the deferral plus manifest reference (or define an equally explicit orchestration contract); update Story 3 tests and Path B so receipt-alone is allowed but never gate-authoritative.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 9d96f86af9: the transaction contract is now explicitly two-stage and acyclic—Story 2 atomically persists a standalone non-gate receipt, then Story 1 separately CAS-validates it and atomically writes deferral plus manifest action; receipt-alone is legal and zero-gate while deferral-alone is invalid.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1249-1280,1324-1328,1420-1429,1542-1565 [high] The lineage-first floor still requires a fresh applicable assessment. When the deferral-bound assessment becomes stale or missing after scope, storyFiles/material, or runtime drift, the claimed deferral simultaneously loses authority, but deferralLineageFloorBlocks can skip because its fresh-applicable precondition is false. A low or round-decayed medium Finding can then fall through to the old non-blocking predicate, contradicting the stated rule that every invalid claimed deferral enters the enforce floor. Define claimed lineage from durable ledger history, not the current assessment/caller; once a committed deferral exists, stale/missing/tampered assessment must project the lineage to missing/unknown and block until a fresh strongly proven non-applicable/disproven verdict or complete repair closure supersedes the obligation. Add low/decayed-medium fixtures for scope/material/runtime drift, a newly minted assessment that omits the old deferral, and no replacement assessment.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 0974481b67: claimed-deferral existence is now derived independently from immutable ledger and canonical chains; missing, stale, tampered or lineage-omitting replacement assessments and scope, story-files, material or runtime drift remain in the first floor until a signed strong non-applicable, duplicate or disproven release or complete repair closure.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1621-1638,1706-1780,1936-1967,2015-2017 — HIGH: the contract text requires the verifier to reject every new gate consumer that bypasses the shared predicate and asserts an acyclic Story 3 -> Story 2 -> Story 1 dependency, but the future Required tests only compare the currently named consumer surfaces and reject Story 2 -> Story 1 imports. No falsifiable mutation test injects a newly registered/phase-allowed consumer that accepts CandidateRoute, standalone FindingRouteReceipt, or historical advisory evidence, and no dependency test rejects Story 3 importing Story 2/1. Therefore all three Story suites can pass while a new lifecycle consumer bypasses the mandatory floor or a reverse lower-layer import creates a cycle. Add contract-verifier mutations for registry/command-policy/phase-allowlist consumer bypasses and dependency fixtures for every forbidden reverse edge, with failure as an enforce stopping condition.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 0974481b67: Required tests now mutate registry, command-policy and phase allow-lists with new direct advisory consumers and inject every forbidden reverse dependency—Story 3 importing Story 2 or 1 and Story 2 importing Story 1; any surviving bypass stops enforce.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:968-985,1392-1398,1692-1695,1764-1777,2142 — HIGH: DeferralExpiryPolicy is promised as signed/versioned gate-consumed policy and each disposition binds policyVersion/policyDigest, but no future Required test mutates or rejects the policy signature, signer authority, policyDigest, version, effectiveAt, horizon constants, or a disposition rebound to a different policy. The existing 7/30-day behavior tests can all pass with a valid V1 fixture while an implementation accepts a forged/stale policy that extends medium or resets a lineage. Add negative/mutation tests proving unsigned/tampered/wrong-authority/wrong-version/not-yet-effective policy and policy-binding mismatch fail closed, and that a policy supersession cannot rebind existing rows or reset firstDeferredAt/count/horizon.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 0974481b67: Story 1 policy tests now mutate signature, authority, digest, version, effectiveAt, horizon constants, hard ceiling and row binding; policy supersession cannot rebind existing rows or reset firstDeferredAt, count or horizon.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:785-813,1209-1219,1497-1504,1771-1776,1865-1868,2142 [medium] The typed progress contract cannot mechanically implement all four advertised ProgressEvidenceKind values. The predecessor baseline and required material-change check cover only target kind/id/scope plus head/material/storyFiles hashes. A legitimate target_test_result, target_delivery_state, or target_status_transition can occur without changing those source/material hashes and is therefore indistinguishable from no progress; conversely an unrelated material/hash change can satisfy the snapshot-difference rule without advancing the routed defect. Define a kind-specific canonical progress projection/baseline (including signed test outcome, delivery/status transition or affected-contract/source delta and its relation to the canonical defect/route), compare that projection rather than only the repository snapshot, and add positive unchanged-code test/delivery/status cases plus negative unrelated-source-change cases. Until then the schema, Story 2 tests, scorecard, risk and acceptance claims of materially progressed renewal are not mutually supported.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 0974481b67: ProgressEvidenceBinding now carries a canonical defect and route-bound kind-specific ProgressProjection for relevant source/contract, defect-bound test receipt, target acceptance/checklist delivery state or permitted defect-work status transition; positive unchanged-code progress and negative unrelated/wrong-subject/no-op cases are required.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:2113-2145 — HIGH: section 11 requires a checked-in finding_rollout_scorecard --json procedure whose computed thresholds authorize warn -> enforce, but none of the three future Story Deliverables/Required tests explicitly owns that command or tests its report computation. The implementation Stories can therefore all pass while the procedure is absent, miscounts numerator/denominator, omits HEAD/window/retry/exclusion metadata, parses protected storage, or promotes on incomplete/tampered events. Assign the scorecard to a Story (normally Story 1) and require deterministic fixture tests for every table row, exact numerator/denominator and threshold/rollback decision, required report metadata, CLI/read-only data boundary, missing/tampered evidence refusal, and enforce-entry refusal when any safety threshold or merged-state prerequisite is unmet.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 0974481b67: Story 1 explicitly owns the checked-in read-only finding_rollout_scorecard JSON aggregator, while Story 2 and 3 expose signed query contracts; deterministic fixtures cover every metric row, exact numerator, denominator, threshold, rollback and metadata, and refuse incomplete, tampered, protected-storage or unmet-prerequisite inputs.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:825-859,1134-1170,1292-1311,1625-1650,1946-1954,2064-2071,2393 [medium] F-021 is only partially closed because the comparison side of ProgressProjection has no immutable source. A renewal supplies projectionDigest and predecessorProjectionDigest, but the initial deferral explicitly has no progressEvidenceBindingDigest and FindingDeferralDisposition stores only a repository targetSnapshotDigest, which the document correctly says is freshness-only and never semantic progress. Since V1 permits exactly one low renewal, that initial row is necessarily the predecessor, yet it contains no kind-specific source/test/delivery/status projection baseline from which the verifier can derive predecessorProjectionDigest. A caller can therefore invent the baseline, or every unchanged-code positive fixture must rely on evidence not represented by the schema. Persist signed kind-specific baseline projection digests (or a target-authorized baseline artifact) with the initial deferral/route for the eligible progress kinds, bind them into dispositionHash/manifest/CAS, and test missing/tampered/wrong-kind baseline plus legitimate unchanged-code and no-op/regressive comparisons. Hash inequality alone must not define semantic progress.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 210da4b610: initial finding-route acceptance now atomically persists a target-authorized CLI/server-derived signed four-kind InitialProgressBaselineSet; deferral and manifest bind exact baseline set ID/hash in the CAS, and renewal derives the same-kind predecessor projection from the immutable set rather than caller input, including signed absent baselines.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1374-1379,1680-1684,1894-1900,2297-2301 [high] F-018 remains internally inconsistent for materialHash-only drift. The ledger-first floor and required tests say scope/story-files/material/runtime drift makes a previously claimed lineage stale or unknown and blocks before status, severity, and round. Section 7.5 still says a materialHash mismatch with matching signed storyFilesHash remains valid with only a re-attestation advisory, while rollback text narrows invalidation to Story-owned material. An implementation can therefore preserve deferral authority across material drift and still satisfy one normative section, defeating the requested always-first drift floor. Define one lineage-specific rule: either material drift blocks until a signed, gate-consumed re-attestation/new fresh assessment is validated, or explicitly narrow every F-018 claim/test to Story-owned/relevant drift and prove shared process/runtime changes cannot affect lineage. The current advisory-versus-blocking ambiguity is not safe for enforce.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 210da4b610: every raw materialHash mismatch on a claimed lineage enters pending_re_attestation and the first blocking floor even when storyFilesHash matches; only current signed L4 proof that Story files and all bound runtime, process-policy, route and canonical dependencies are unaffected restores valid, while host self-classification or invalid/related/unknown proof remains blocked.

findings.desc: Process-fact enforcement does not mechanically preserve the new baseline artifacts' declared non-gate boundary. FindingRouteReceipt encodes evidenceAuthority.gateEvidence=false (lines 734-741), but InitialProgressBaseline and InitialProgressBaselineSet expose signed target-authorized artifacts without an equivalent non-gate authority marker (lines 830-886). More importantly, the required registry/command-policy/phase-allowlist mutation suite only injects direct consumers of CandidateRoute, standalone FindingRouteReceipt, and historical advisory/candidate data (lines 1998-2002; repeated at 2324-2326 and 2441-2444), omitting InitialProgressBaseline/InitialProgressBaselineSet. Therefore an implementation could register a lifecycle gate that consumes a standalone baseline/set directly even though the prose and scorecard assert zero standalone gate delta. Add explicit baseline/set non-gate authority to the artifact contract and mutation fixtures that fail every direct baseline/baseline-set gate consumer; preserve Story 1 as the sole L4 consumer through exact final receipt+baseline CAS and the shared predicate.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by cc5c996b61: every InitialProgressBaseline entry and InitialProgressBaselineSet now signs and hashes evidenceAuthority profile progress_baseline, target_route_semantic_only and gateEvidence false; registry, command-policy and phase-allowlist mutation tests reject direct blocker, pass or unblock consumption, marker removal or profile impersonation, leaving only Story 1 exact-CAS-derived signed L4 state gate-eligible.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1599-1607,1633-1657,2180-2182,2699 — Missing/stale applicability leaves a Round-3 verified high Finding able to bypass the promised fail-closed safety floor. The mandatory-repair floor is created only for a fresh `applicable` assessment, while a missing/unsigned/tampered/mismatched/stale assessment with no claimed deferral falls back to the previous predicate. That predicate makes `high` advisory from Round 3 (`packages/main/src/core/advisory.ts:52-75`; `packages/main/src/core/guard-utils.ts:50-56`). Consequently a verified open high Finding can become non-blocking precisely because classification is absent or invalid, contradicting the assertions that unknown high/critical is never downgraded and that missing required classification blocks. Make verified high/critical missing/stale/invalid assessments enter the pre-round mandatory-repair floor, or explicitly narrow and reconcile the safety contract; add a Round-3 high plus missing/stale/unsigned assessment adversarial fixture.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 37d941607e. The shared gate contract now places verified open high/critical Findings with missing, stale, unsigned, tampered, mismatched, incomplete, or unknown required applicability assessments into a non-decaying mandatory-repair floor before round/advisory policy; the only high/critical exception is a fresh strongly proven non-applicable verdict. The applicability pseudo-code no longer falls through to the previous predicate, legacy enforce behavior is explicit, Story 1 acceptance adds a round-3 verified-open-high fixture for each invalid/missing assessment plus a fresh-valid non-applicable control, and the scorecard fail-closed metric names the same matrix. Evidence commands: git show --check --stat HEAD; rg -n for the floor/pseudo-code/fixture/scorecard clauses in docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md; commit author is lattice-implementer.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1599-1625,1643-1650,1667-1670,2151-2156 — The new missing/invalid-assessment floor has no release transition for a later fresh strong non-applicable verdict. Missing or invalid assessment now creates a non-decaying mandatory-repair floor, while lines 1618-1622 say the only clearing state is `closure_proven` with a complete repair chain. The later statement that a fresh `pre_existing_unaffected`, `out_of_scope`, or `duplicate` verdict does not create the floor only handles a clean initial control; it does not supersede an already active `required` record created while assessment was absent. Therefore an open verified high Finding first observed without an assessment can remain permanently blocked and require repair even after its independent strong non-applicable proof succeeds. Define whether assessment-invalidity is a transient pre-round fail-closed projection or add a signed release/supersession path limited to that reason, and add a missing-to-fresh-non-applicable transition fixture rather than only paired initial states.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit 6189f4b025. The shared gate now derives assessmentIntegrityFloorBlocks before mandatoryRepairFloorBlocks and ordinary round policy. Section 7.1 states assessment integrity is transient, is not a MandatoryRepairClassification or confirmed applicability, and requires no Red-to-Green repair closure: later fresh signed strong pre_existing_unaffected, out_of_scope, or duplicate proof releases it; fresh applicable high/critical converts it to mandatory repair; weak or invalid assessment remains blocking. Story 1 adds all three transition fixtures plus clean initial controls. Verification: git show --check --stat 6189f4b025 passed; structural document audit confirmed floor order, release/convert/remain transitions, closure-only qualification, and controls.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1603-1605,1643-1646,2151-2156,2719 — The fail-closed qualification matrix is not internally identical. The normative prose includes an `incomplete` required assessment, but the pseudo-code case and Story 1 adversarial fixture omit `incomplete`. The scorecard numerator and denominator count only high/critical `unknown` cases, while its collection and rollback columns claim missing, stale, unsigned, tampered, mismatched, unknown, and invalid assessments. A future verifier or aggregator can therefore omit the incomplete case or report 100% using a denominator that excludes invalid variants. Use one exact named state set in the predicate, fixture, and scorecard numerator/denominator, including `incomplete`, and keep the fresh-valid non-applicable control outside that denominator.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit 6189f4b025. The exact invalid set is now missing, stale, unsigned, tampered, mismatched, incomplete, unknown across the type model, shared gate pseudocode, Story 1 acceptance and required tests, and the scorecard numerator, denominator, collection, thresholds, and rollback. Required tests cover high and critical at round 3 across all seven variants, exclude fresh valid controls, and include release, conversion, and remain-blocking transitions. Verification: git show --check --stat 6189f4b025 passed; structural document audit confirmed every exact-set and scorecard binding.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1053-1073,1563-1584,2062-2115,2177-2180,2214-2217 — HIGH doc-contract inconsistency: the plan now defines a signed verifier-derived gate-consumed AssessmentIntegrityState with release/convert/remain states, but isDynamicFindingBlocking neither accepts nor consumes that state; assessmentIntegrityFloorBlocks receives only raw assessmentState. The detailed L4 process-fact/registry list then omits AssessmentIntegrityState, its verifier/reader, exact REQUIRED_ASSESSMENT_INVALID semantics, and release/convert/remain mutation coverage, despite the Story 1 deliverable saying both floors receive contract-verifier coverage. A future implementation can satisfy the enumerated registry contract while never mechanically binding or consuming the signed integrity projection, letting per-consumer derivations disagree or bypass the round-3 floor. Add assessmentIntegrityState to the shared predicate contract (or explicitly make the helper the sole registered derivation and remove the unused signed artifact), and explicitly register/verifier-test its exact seven-state set and strong-non-applicable release/fresh-applicable conversion/invalid-remain transitions across every blocker consumer.

docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:2457-2460 and :2518-2521 still define the Story 1 Round-3 matrix and required fail-closed behavior as the old seven-state set, omitting newly introduced re_attestation_required and expired. This conflicts with REQUIRED_ASSESSMENT_INVALID (nine states) and the Section 11 scorecard denominator at :3090, so required test coverage no longer mechanically proves the two new invalid states block. Update both required-test bullets to the exact nine-state set and require their round-3 fail-closed fixtures.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: all Story 1 required-test and boundary summaries now use the canonical nine invalid states, including re_attestation_required and expired, and require the high/critical round-3 fail-closed Cartesian fixtures.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1027-1066,1576-1579 — HIGH: Assessment.acceptedRoute includes receiptHash/sourceAssessmentHash inside the bytes covered by assessmentHash, while the receipt source subjectHash and manifest contract must equal that same final assessmentHash. The receipt therefore needs the assessment hash before the assessment can include/sign the receipt hash, creating an undefined hash fixed point. Define a two-stage immutable assessment-proposal digest or an explicit hash-exclusion/canonicalization rule; otherwise accepted-route assessments and defer-with-proof cannot be constructed.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: accepted-route construction now uses an immutable signed assessmentProposalDigest before target receipt issuance; final assessmentHash is computed after receipt binding with explicit hash exclusions, removing the Assessment/receipt fixed point while preserving exact final CAS bindings.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1537-1561,1606-1614 — HIGH: GateEvaluationSnapshot binds record/digest heads but has no evaluatedAt, trusted-clock binding, or earliest-expiry boundary, and commit-time CAS only detects changed bytes. An assessment or route can cross expiresAt after preflight while every CAS head remains unchanged, so the stale snapshot can still authorize a transition. Bind trusted evaluation time/expiry and recheck time-based validity at commit, including replay/expiry race tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: GateEvaluationSnapshot now binds evaluatedAt, trustedClockDigest, earliestBoundExpiry and commitDeadline; transition commit rechecks trusted time and every expiry, with expiry-boundary, replay, clock and preflight-to-commit race fixtures.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:2457-2464,2518-2521 — HIGH: Story 1 Required tests twice call a seven-value subset the exact required-assessment set, omitting re_attestation_required and expired, while REQUIRED_ASSESSMENT_INVALID and the scorecard define nine states. This contradictory acceptance contract can ship without testing two fail-closed states. Both exact lists and the projection statement must reference all nine canonical states.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: the three stale seven-state lists were replaced with the exact nine-state REQUIRED_ASSESSMENT_INVALID set and the projection/test contract explicitly covers re_attestation_required and expired.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:2883-2890 — MEDIUM: the Safe sequence says step 2 implements/accepts Story 2 on 3A and that both authoritative contracts pass, then step 3 again says to implement/accept Story 2 authoritative identity/lineage. This duplicates and contradicts the milestone boundary. State step 2 as 3B plus read-only Story 2/Story 1 work, then make Story 2 authoritative delivery a single later step, or explicitly allow 3B and authoritative Story 2 in parallel without repeating it.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: the safe sequence now has one Story 2 authoritative delivery step after Story 3A, permits only read-only Story 1/2 prototypes alongside Story 3B, and removes the duplicate contradictory Story 2 implementation step.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:687-693,1135-1178,1251-1298,1301-1340,1343-1403 — HIGH: The new identity contract says every signed reference must use globally unique FindingRef/recordId to prevent display-ID aliasing, but four gate-consumed signed artifacts (MandatoryRepairClassification, MaterialDriftReattestation, DeferralLineageState, and FindingDeferralDisposition) still identify the Finding only by storyId+findingId. A reused/legacy-aliased display tuple therefore has no immutable recordId in the signed bytes, while AssessmentIntegrityState and manifest use FindingRef, leaving two incompatible identity authorities across the same gate. Convert every gate-relevant Finding reference to FindingRef (and bind its exact record/version/hash as appropriate), then add alias/reuse/legacy-binding mutation tests; otherwise the advertised global identity and CAS safety are not implementable.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: MandatoryRepairClassification, MaterialDriftReattestation, DeferralLineageState and FindingDeferralDisposition now sign FindingRef plus required finding hash/version bindings; alias, reused display ID and legacy-binding mutation tests fail closed.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1069-1075,1828-1843,1877-1899,2149-2155,2466-2473 — HIGH: not_reproduced_under_current_witness is newly modeled as a current-evidence verdict that may be non-blocking, but the verifier-derived integrity state machine and its required controls release a prior missing/invalid high-critical assessment only for pre_existing_unaffected, out_of_scope, or duplicate. Thus the same fresh signed not-reproduced assessment can be non-blocking when clean-initial yet remain latched blocking after missing→fresh, unless a consumer invents an undocumented fourth release path; either outcome contradicts the derived/no-second-authority contract. Specify its owner/routing and strong-proof requirements, include it consistently in release/remain semantics and clean-initial/transition fixtures (or explicitly make it always blocking), and bind that choice in the registered state machine.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: not_reproduced_under_current_witness now has explicit current-witness strong-proof and owner/route requirements and is consistently included in both clean-initial and missing-to-fresh integrity release paths and their registered state-machine fixtures.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:2306-2308,2333-2337,2578-2580,2852-2854,2913-2917,3210 — MEDIUM: The revised authoritative DAG distinguishes Story 3A and 3B and requires 3B to import 3A only and Story 2 to import 3A, but the process-fact contract, required tests, and risk stop-rule still assert only the old umbrella Story 3 -> Story 2 -> Story 1 mutation graph. Those tests do not independently reject 3A importing 3B or Story 2 importing 3B (and do not state the allowed 3B->3A edge), so a cyclic or over-coupled milestone graph can pass the promised enforce prerequisite. Update every mechanical dependency fixture/acceptance statement to the same explicit 3A/3B/Story 2/Story 1 edge matrix and mutate each forbidden reverse edge independently.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: process-fact, required-test and risk contracts now use the explicit 3A/3B/Story 2/Story 1 allowed-edge matrix and independently mutate every forbidden reverse or cross-layer import before enforce.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1496-1512,1565-1573,2931-2936 — MEDIUM: migration appends a signed LegacyFindingIdentityBinding but FindingLedgerReceipt.operation has no append_legacy_identity_binding operation, and the prose incorrectly exempts the binding as commit metadata to avoid receipt recursion. The binding is gate-relevant identity state, not the ledger receipt itself; without a first-class idempotent/CAS ledger operation, concurrent first-read/backfill can create duplicate recordIds or an unreceipted identity mapping. Add an explicit atomic idempotent binding operation; only FindingLedgerReceipt itself should be non-recursively receipted.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: LegacyFindingIdentityBinding is now written through append_legacy_identity_binding with tuple/hash CAS, idempotency and atomic receipt semantics; only FindingLedgerReceipt itself is exempt from receipt recursion.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:3048-3050,3107-3108 — MEDIUM: the scorecard says genuine repair must be reported and never credited as Dynamic Finding savings, but Manual Finding-operation reduction counts avoided repair-related operations toward its >=50% promotion threshold. This permits the efficiency claim to be inflated by repair work the contract explicitly excludes. Limit that numerator to classification/triage/adjudication/reproduction/routing/assessment workflow operations and report genuine repair separately.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: the manual-operation reduction numerator excludes genuine repair work and measures classification, triage, adjudication, reproduction, routing and assessment operations; repair is reported separately and never credited as Dynamic Finding savings.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1489-1512,1565-1573,2923-2936,3275-3277 — HIGH: LegacyFindingIdentityBinding is an authoritative signed migration record, but the ledger operation union has no append/bind-legacy-identity operation and migration calls it unreceipted commit metadata. That leaves its tuple→recordId mapping outside the stated atomic/idempotent/receipted mutation boundary, with no exact CAS or replay contract for two concurrent first reads/backfills; the mapping intended to prevent aliasing can itself fork into two authorities. Give it an explicit Story 3A ledger operation/receipt, idempotency key and tuple/hash CAS (while still excluding only FindingLedgerReceipt self-recursion), and add concurrent bind/collision/retry/crash fixtures.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 93ab5605b4: legacy tuple-to-recordId binding is a first-class Story 3A ledger operation with exact CAS, idempotency, receipt, retry, crash and concurrent first-read/backfill fixtures, preventing the migration mapping from forking.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1025-1032,1382-1386,1482,1586-1592,1610-1620 — HIGH targeted re-review of 93ab5605b4: the new two-stage assessmentProposalDigest construction is contradicted by surviving routeReceiptSourceAssessmentHash / expectedRouteReceiptSourceAssessmentHash fields and the rule that this value equals expectedAssessmentHash and receipt.subjectHash. That reinstates the final-assessment/receipt hash fixed point the new paragraph says is forbidden. The proposal-digest definition also says it covers every assessment input except acceptedRoute, assessmentHash and signature but does not explicitly exclude assessmentProposalDigest itself. Replace every route/deferral/manifest/source-assessment binding with the proposal digest, bind final assessmentHash separately, and define an acyclic canonical field set that excludes the proposal digest field itself.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by d26fb86fe9: proposal digest canonicalization excludes itself, proposal signature, accepted route and final hashes; Story 2 receipt binds only the signed proposal digest, while the final assessment independently signs the exact receipt tuple and never flows its final hash back into the receipt.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1543-1572,1628-1639 — HIGH targeted re-review of 93ab5605b4: GateEvaluationSnapshot makes earliestBoundExpiryAt optional and never requires the verifier to derive it as the minimum of every bound assessment, route, deferral and policy expiry. A signed snapshot can omit it or use a later time; commit-time clock recheck then has no effective boundary while record CAS heads remain unchanged. Require the field whenever any input is expiry-bound, derive and verify the complete minimum under the ledger snapshot, and add omission/later-value plus exact-boundary and replay race fixtures.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by d26fb86fe9: GateEvaluationSnapshot now carries a signed expiryClosure over complete expiring-input enumeration, canonical earliest expiry or explicit signed empty no-expiry state, trusted clock policy and commit deadline; commit re-enumerates and rejects omission, forged-late values, boundaries and replay races.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:2554-2557,3325-3327 — HIGH targeted re-review of 93ab5605b4: two normative Story 1/merged-acceptance clauses still call {missing, stale, unsigned, tampered, mismatched, incomplete, unknown} the exact invalid set, omitting re_attestation_required and expired. This still conflicts with REQUIRED_ASSESSMENT_INVALID and the nine-state matrix, so F030/F033 are not fully repaired despite one required-test occurrence being updated. Replace both residual lists with the canonical nine-state set or reference the named constant exclusively.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by d26fb86fe9 and d260eccd08: all required-test and acceptance-summary invalid-state lists now use the exact nine-state set including re_attestation_required and expired; targeted multiline residue scan is empty.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:2554-2557,3325-3333 — HIGH: 93ab5605b4 updates the first Story 1 matrix to nine states but leaves the second required-test contract and the implementation acceptance summary at the old seven-state exact set, still omitting re_attestation_required and expired. This means F-030/F-033 are only partially fixed and the plan can still satisfy one authoritative acceptance list without proving both new states fail closed. Make both remaining lists reference the canonical nine-state set (or REQUIRED_ASSESSMENT_INVALID) and include the round-3 fixtures.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by d26fb86fe9 and d260eccd08: the remaining seven-state required-test and summary residues were replaced with REQUIRED_ASSESSMENT_INVALID's exact nine states, with high/critical round-3 fail-closed coverage.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1025-1067,1382-1385,1479-1482,1610-1621,1982-1998,2322-2324 — HIGH: The proposed F-031 two-stage construction is still not constructible as written. assessmentProposalDigest is itself an AssessmentEnvelope input but the canonical exclusion list omits that field, and there is no separate proposal record/signature even though Story 2 must accept an assessor-signed immutable proposal before the final assessment exists. In addition, deferral/manifest schema and CAS/process-fact prose still bind sourceAssessmentHash/final expectedAssessmentHash instead of sourceAssessmentProposalDigest, recreating the final-hash cycle or two competing bindings. Define a separately signed proposal artifact/digest that excludes its own digest/signature, replace every route/deferral/manifest/CAS field with the proposal-digest binding where intended, and mutation-test proposal/final divergence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by d26fb86fe9: the two-stage proposal has an independently signed, non-self-referential digest; receipt/deferral/manifest/CAS fields uniformly bind source assessment proposal digest plus separate final assessment hash, eliminating fixed-point and double-authority remnants.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1543-1571,1628-1640,2625-2628 — HIGH: The F-032 repair adds trusted-clock fields but leaves earliestBoundExpiryAt optional and never states that the verifier must derive it as the minimum expiry of every assessment/route/deferral/policy input or reject omission/mismatch when any bound input expires. The required gate-snapshot fixtures still cover only digest/scope races and do not mutate evaluatedAt, trustedClockDigest, clockPolicyDigest, omitted/late/forged earliest expiry, clock rollback, or expiry between preflight and commit. A snapshot can therefore omit the boundary and pass unchanged-byte CAS after expiry. Make expiry presence/derivation fail-closed and add the full clock/expiry race matrix to Story 1 acceptance and rollout qualification.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by d26fb86fe9 and d260eccd08: expiry closure cannot be omitted; nonempty inputs require the mechanically derived minimum, empty inputs require signed noExpiry, and Story 1 tests mutate enumeration, forged minimum, clock/policy drift, exact boundary, preflight-to-commit expiry and replay.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1890-1894,2501-2509,2525-2528,3132 — HIGH: F-036 is only partially integrated. Story 1 transition prose now includes not_reproduced_under_current_witness, but the mandatory-floor exclusion bullet and rollout scorecard clean-initial control set still enumerate only pre_existing_unaffected/out_of_scope/duplicate. Consequently enforce qualification can omit the new verdict’s clean-initial control and does not prove clean-initial equals missing→fresh, leaving the original path-dependent latch risk outside the scorecard. Include target-bound not_reproduced_under_current_witness in every integrity-release/non-mandatory statement and in the scorecard transition plus clean-initial numerator/denominator/rollback fixtures.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by d26fb86fe9, d260eccd08 and a6f3d3b0fe: target-bound strongly proven not_reproduced_under_current_witness now has consistent assessment-integrity release, mandatory-floor exclusion, clean-initial/transition, required-test and scorecard controls while never releasing an independent claimed-deferral lineage.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1019-1068,1619-1630,2449-2465,2690-2703,2976-2979 [high] F-041/F-045 remain incomplete: proposalSignature was added only to the final AssessmentEnvelope, whose schema still requires final assessmentHash/signature and whose verdict-specific proposal fields live outside the envelope. There is no independently constructible/persisted pre-route proposal/attachment schema, canonical field list, signer authority, or verifier/negative-test contract for Story 2 to validate before issuing the receipt. Treating the digest as opaque cannot prove which verdict/basis/current-witness payload the target accepted; importing Story 1 assessment types/verifier would violate the declared Story 2 -> 3A-only DAG. Define a lower/shared signed proposal attachment contract (including exact union payload, signer authority, canonical exclusions and durable lookup/verification) that Story 2 can consume without Story 1, then mutation-test proposal/final divergence and wrong proposal signer/signature.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 13ef26bf0e: a standalone immutable discriminated FindingAssessmentProposal now has canonical signed payload, signer authority and Story 3A append_assessment_proposal persistence/receipt plus a shared verifier/query API usable by Story 2 without importing Story 1; route and final assessment verify exact proposal lookup/digest and reject divergence.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:3348-3350 — HIGH: the final implementation acceptance still defines the assessment-integrity floor with only seven states and omits re_attestation_required and expired, contradicting the normative REQUIRED_ASSESSMENT_INVALID nine-state set at lines 1851-1854 and the immediately following claim that all nine states are mutation-tested. An implementation can satisfy this acceptance bullet while failing open for either omitted state. Make the acceptance predicate consume the exact named nine-state constant/set, and require both omitted cells in the final acceptance fixture matrix.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 6ec47f30f6: Section 15 final acceptance now consumes the named REQUIRED_ASSESSMENT_INVALID exact nine-state set and explicitly requires blocking re_attestation_required and expired cells in the final acceptance matrix.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1401-1403,1571-1578,1647-1653 — HIGH: FindingDeferralDisposition has a binding expiresAt, but GateEvaluationSnapshot expiryClosure only says its reader enumerates expiring assessment, receipt, policy, and runtime inputs; deferrals are absent. A valid claimed deferral can therefore cross its expiresAt between preflight and commit with unchanged record bytes and escape the canonical earliest-expiry CAS, despite the stated exact-boundary/race guarantee. Include every active deferral/lineage expiry in expiringInputIds and earliestBoundExpiryAt and add omission, forged-later-minimum, exact-boundary, and preflight-to-commit race fixtures for deferral expiry.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 13ef26bf0e: GateEvaluationSnapshot expiryClosure entries now bind type, record ID, record hash and expiresAt and mechanically enumerate every active FindingDeferralDisposition and DeferralLineageState; deferral omission, forged-later minimum, exact boundary and preflight-to-commit races fail closed.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1545-1581,1638-1653 [high] F-042/F-046 remain incomplete: FindingDeferralDisposition.expiresAt is a gate-bound expiry, but the new expiryClosure rule mechanically enumerates only assessment, receipt, policy, and runtime inputs and never names deferral/disposition expiry. A signed snapshot can therefore omit the active deferral expiry while keeping the listed set internally consistent, allowing unchanged-byte commit CAS after the deferral boundary. Require enumeration/minimum derivation over every active deferral/disposition expiry as well, bind its exact ID/hash in the snapshot input set, and add an omission/boundary race fixture specifically for deferral expiry.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 13ef26bf0e: active deferral/disposition and lineage expiries are first-class typed expiryClosure inputs included in the canonical minimum and bound by ID/hash/time, with dedicated omission and unchanged-byte boundary-race fixtures.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:3375-3381 [high] F-047 remains partially unfixed in the final implementation acceptance: the normative release/non-mandatory rule again enumerates only pre_existing_unaffected, out_of_scope, and duplicate, omitting target-bound strong not_reproduced_under_current_witness. That permits an implementation to satisfy the final acceptance summary while latching this valid verdict into the temporary integrity/mandatory floor, contrary to the union, transition tests, and scorecard. Add the current-witness verdict with its strong target-bound proof/owner-route qualification here while preserving the separate rule that it cannot release a claimed-deferral or existing mandatory-repair lineage.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 13ef26bf0e: Section 15 final acceptance explicitly includes target-bound strong not_reproduced_under_current_witness with live accepted owner/route and signed current negative witness/policy digests, while forbidding it from releasing claimed lineage or an existing mandatory-repair floor.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md:1098-1102,1669-1679,2036-2067 — HIGH: the new two-stage proposal/final contract is not constructible for the plan’s own defer-with-proof path. AssessmentRouteBinding explicitly makes acceptedRoute impossible when verdict=applicable, but Path B requires a verified applicable low/medium assessment plus a target-accepted finding_route receipt, and the canonicalization paragraph says the final Story 1 assessment consumes and signs that exact receipt tuple. A conforming final applicable assessment therefore cannot carry the receipt the final verifier is required to validate; implementations must either violate the schema or silently move the route binding outside the promised final-assessment contract. Define an applicable-with-acceptedRoute variant for deferral (while retaining route-free ordinary applicable assessments), or state and test that the final applicable assessment is route-free and that only the signed deferral/manifest binds the proposal receipt tuple.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 59698dda90: AssessmentRouteBinding now has constructible applicable repair_current and applicable defer_with_proof variants; the former forbids route, the latter requires the exact accepted receipt, while mandatory eligibility independently rejects high/critical and protected-surface deferral and fixtures cover every illegal combination.
